hints: Look carefully at the word mitotic, not just cell cycle. Which option names a stage inside nuclear division itself?
Recall the four stages of mitosis in order: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase. Which option is on that short list?
walkthrough:
**Separate mitosis from the cell cycle**

Think of the cell cycle as the big picture. It is interphase plus mitosis plus cytokinesis.

Mitosis itself is much narrower. It is only nuclear division.

**List what belongs to mitosis**

Mitosis has four stages you must know in order: prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase.

Anaphase is when sister chromatids separate to opposite poles. That is right in the middle of mitosis.

**Sort the other options out**

DNA replication happens in S phase of interphase, not in mitosis. Interphase and cytokinesis are parts of the whole cell cycle, but they are not parts of mitosis.

So only anaphase is part of the mitotic (mitosis) phase.

options.A: Correct. Anaphase is one of the four stages of mitosis, so it is part of the mitotic phase.
options.B: Cytokinesis is division of the cytoplasm after nuclear division. It is part of the cell cycle but not part of mitosis.
options.C: DNA replication occurs during S phase of interphase to double the DNA before mitosis, not during mitosis.
options.D: Interphase is the long growth phase of the cell cycle before mitosis, not a stage within mitosis.
